title: The quick check passes before a commit and fails after
what: `bin/ci --quick` in a worktree with uncommitted changes either reads the same text the gate will (the working tree), or says in its last line that it checked the last commit, not the edits.
why: taste: core-tests-not-in-gate (23 Oct). Tests that read committed text (committed_items, committed_text in tests/test_queue.py) see the old commit while a worker loops on uncommitted edits, so `bin/ci --quick` is green in the worktree and the gate on the commit is red; one ~8 min gate run and a fixer round were spent on it. It repeats on every change that touches a file such a test reads.
failing_case: On wt/core-tests-not-in-gate, bin/ci with the edit uncommitted: green; the same edit committed: TestSeedItems.test_f14_a_where_line_names_the_line_the_item_talks_about fails ('*inject-addition*' not found).
pass_cases: An edit that breaks a committed-text test fails `bin/ci --quick` before the commit as it does after it, or the run states it checked HEAD only.
